St. Benedict of Nursia

Saints

Saint Benedict of Nursia

St. Benedict of Nursia · St. Benedict of Norcia · St. Benedict of Monte Cassino

Period
c.480–547 (OCA chronology)
Region
Nursia; Subiaco; Monte Cassino, Italy
Titles / vocation
Monastic · Abbot · Teacher
Commemoration
March 14

Introduction

Saint Benedict was an Italian monk and abbot whose Rule helped shape Western monastic life. He is commemorated in the Orthodox calendar on March 14.

Read the published life [1]

Death / martyrdom

Monastic repose,547 according to the OCA life

Read circumstances and sources

Background

The OCA places his birth in Nursia in 480. Sent to study in Rome, he chose an ascetic life. A hermit guided him into monasticism, and he lived for a time in a cave at Subiaco.

[1] Official ecclesiastical biography / teaching / commemoration · Opening paragraphs on birth, Rome and Subiaco

Life and notable events

Disciples gathered around him, and he organized monastic communities with experienced leaders. Opposition accompanied his efforts. He later founded Monte Cassino, which became an important center of learning and manuscript preservation.

[1] Official ecclesiastical biography / teaching / commemoration · Paragraphs on twelve communities and Monte Cassino

Death and martyrdom

The ecclesiastical life dates Saint Benedict’s repose to 547. It does not describe martyrdom. It identifies the second book of Saint Gregory’s Dialogues as the principal narrative source for his life.

[1] Official ecclesiastical biography / teaching / commemoration · Final paragraphs on repose and principal source

Writings and legacy

His Rule draws on the desert monastic tradition and Saint John Cassian. It organizes common life, work, obedience, formation, and the abbot’s responsibilities. His Orthodox commemoration belongs to the shared history of the first-millennium Church.

[1] Official ecclesiastical biography / teaching / commemoration · Paragraphs on the Rule and its influences
